header:
Date: 2025-06-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Atlas Infra), Leah Kim (Atlas Product), Danielle Park (Atlas Security), Tom Hsu (Atlas SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on access handoff, infra readiness and quick performance readout. Atlas and Redwood aligned on next infra items; Redwood to provide bench runbook and example tests; security questions (SOC2/KMS/audit logs) to be clarified by Danielle; plan for infra-only smoke test and then application-level bench next week.
topics: Access credentials and gateway rules, VPC peering and egress, test tokens and priming, bench results recap (p50/p99), model variants and fallback policy, KMS / audit logs, timeline for canary runs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run 45ish mins. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Sam: Sam here, Infra.
[00:15] Leah: Leah, product.
[00:18] Danielle: Danielle from security.
[00:21] Tom: Tom, SRE.
[00:23] Jordan: Great. So agenda, access handoff, quick readout of the small bench you ran last week, and then next infra gating items. Priya will do the bench runbook portion.
[00:36] Priya: Hi all. Quick note on the bench — the run you gave us on 6/20, we re-ran with the quantized variant and got p50 around 82ms and p99 around 320ms for the 2k token prompt on our dedicated config. That lined up-ish with the spreadsheet but we saw higher p99 when requests came in bursty pattern. Might be batching config.
[01:02] Tom: Those numbers sound good for hosted, but our SLA target is 200ms p99 for the interactive feature. I'm curious about steady-state vs cold starts.
[01:12] Marco: Right, cold starts due to KV cache miss; once the KV cache is primed p99 drops significantly — we saw ~190ms in a warmed run. Note that our internal kernel selection had pairings that increased tail latency on one of the GPUs.
[01:30] Sam: Quick infra question — for the private pilot we need VPC peering details. Do you need static IPs from us or can you accept NATed egress?
[01:40] Jordan: We can support both. For quickest path do a controlled NAT egress to Redwood control plane and we'll provide the IP ranges. If you want VPC peering for no egress, that's fine but will take a day or two extra.
[01:52] Danielle: On security, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, KMS integration for customer keys, and audit log retention policy. Also, SSO SAML for Console access.
[02:03] Priya: We have SOC 2 doc set, KMS is supported for Private deployments; for hosted we offer bring-your-own-key with HSM integration for dedicated tiers. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM, retention configurable. We'll share links.
[02:20] Leah: Is there any PII or PHI exfiltration risk with your control plane? Our compliance folks are worried.
[02:27] Jordan: Short answer, control plane only handles orchestration metadata. Payload handling is opt-in for hosted; for Private we keep traffic in your VPC. We'll send the data flow diagram.
[02:39] Tom: On credentials — how are test tokens rotated? We don't want long-lived creds in CI.
[02:45] Marco: We give short-lived tokens (1 hour by default) and an API to programmatically refresh. For the POC we can provision service tokens with limited scope.
[02:56] Sam: Ok, so immediate gating items from infra: allow outbound to Redwood IP ranges, or give us peering contact. We'll need a specific list.
[03:04] Jordan: I'll put the IP ranges + peering contact in the follow-up email.
[03:08] Priya: Bench runbook highlights: example curl, node client snippet, priming KV cache step, and how to set batch size. We'll include a small script to produce synthetic burst traffic so you can reproduce p99 spikes.
[03:26] Leah: In your last run you mentioned switching between full and quantized models. Can you clarify when fallback happens? We want predictable quality.
[03:33] Marco: Yes, fallback is policy-based. We can route by latency SLO — when latency or capacity is constrained we'll fallback to a smaller quantized variant. Quality regression is usually minimal for short prompts; we'll tie it to your eval prompt set.
[03:50] Danielle: Also please note we need all storage encrypted at rest with our KMS and logs pushed to our logging account. Any ingestion retention must be 30 days by default.
[04:01] Priya: Noted, we'll confirm the retention defaults and KMS mode for hosted vs private.
[04:07] Tom: For the smoke test, we'd like infra-only steps first (no product traffic). What do you need from our side?
[04:13] Jordan: Provide VPC CIDR and a point of contact to open firewall rules. We'll do an infra smoke test — control plane reachability and short-lived token auth — then we'll escalate to an app-level bench with Leah's team.
[04:27] Sam: We had a failed attempt earlier because the gateway needed an outbound rule to S3 for the bootstrap. Is that still required?
[04:34] Marco: That's the bootstrap path for certain models and asset prefetching. If you block S3, we'll need to mirror assets into your VPC. We'll document that.
[04:45] Leah: On timeline — when can we expect the infra smoke and then app bench?
[04:50] Jordan: If we get VPC details by 6/30, infra smoke test could be 6/30 or 7/1 and app-level bench early next week.
[04:59] Danielle: Any third-party subprocessor list for hosted? We need a data flow map.
[05:05] Jordan: Yes, we'll share the subprocessor list and data flow diagram; note sometimes vendor names are munged in auto transcript so expect clean docs.
[05:16] Priya: Quick technical aside — when you saw p99 spikes, the main lever is batch size and queue depth. Also, prefix KV caching and warm-starting reduces token generation cost. We'll include suggested batch/queue settings in the runbook.
[05:35] Tom: Are there any known regressions with model quantization on our workload types (few-shot prompts, long contexts)?
[05:43] Marco: For long contexts >2k tokens we recommend the non-quantized variant; quantization helps cost but may slightly reduce long-form coherence. We'll propose a two-tier policy: quality-critical routes pinned to full model, everything else to quantized.
[05:59] Leah: Good. On the vendor side, we've also been trialing Bedrock for some tasks. How do you compare?
[06:07] Jordan: We compete on predictable latency and cost controls — our routing and caching usually gives lower per-token cost at scale. But every customer's profile differs, we'll provide a trimmed benchmark to compare.
[06:18] Danielle: Any docs for encryption in transit and at rest? Need TLS details and key lifecycle.
[06:23] Marco: We'll attach our security brief; TLS 1.2+ enforced on control/data plane, KMS support for key rotation.
[06:30] Priya: Also, quick note about metrics: send us a representative traffic pattern for 10k qps? We'll show how autoscaling behaves.
[06:38] Tom: Not 10k yet, more like steady 100-200 qps — but we can simulate bursts.
[06:43] Priya: Perfect. We'll include a synthetic burst script.
[06:47] Jordan: Any blockers from your side?
[06:49] Sam: Primary blocker is getting the NAT egress rules approved; security wants KMS and the SOC 2 doc before full peering.
[06:57] Danielle: Yes, plus we want a statement on logs retention and how to disable payload snapshotting.
[07:03] Marco: You can disable payload snapshotting on the tenant config; we'll send instructions.
[07:09] Leah: Action recap?
[07:11] Jordan: I'll summarize. Jordan to send IP ranges, pilot pricing, SOC2 link; Priya to send runbook and scripts; Priya/Marco to include model variant guidance; Tom to open firewall change and share VPC CIDR; Danielle to confirm retention and KMS constraints.
[07:28] Sam: Sounds good.
[07:30] Jordan: Any other Qs?
[07:32] Leah: Quick one — do you have a mock canary policy example for rollouts?
[07:36] Marco: Yes, we'll share a canary template: 5% traffic for 24 hours, automatic rollback on error or latency spike.
[07:44] Jordan: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the documents and schedule the infra smoke test.
[07:50] Danielle: Thanks.
[07:52] Meeting ends.
